title: Dedicated rate commitments and deferred burst policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: enterprise customers buying Dedicated capacity require deterministic monthly throughput entitlements while retaining some burstability for spiky workloads. Current SLA templates either (a) guarantee a flat tokens-per-minute floor that is expensive to guarantee during AZ-failures, or (b) offer vague language around "bursts" that legal and sales cannot operationalize. This ticket proposes a precise definition for rate commitments, an error-budget computation tied to rolling quantiles, and a 'deferred burst' policy (time-windowed crediting and prioritization) that preserves availability, bounds cost exposure, and maps cleanly to billing credits.
background: Context: follow-on from FY25 SLA rewrite work and incidents in 2026-01 where two Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput during autoscaler throttling (incident INC-2026-01-17). Existing PM and Legal drafts are scattered: Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DED/pages/Throughput+Commitments, Sales template: drive.google.com/drive/folders/Redwood/Sales/SLA-templates, and draft contract language in PM-72011 and PM-7124. Engineering has a prototype measurement pipeline (ENG-20421) and an autoscale feature flag branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1987.
proposal_summary: 1) Define three throughput bands (Committed, Sizable Burst, Elastic Best-Effort) measured on a rolling 1h window with 95th/50th quantile bounds. 2) Error budget computed on a per-customer basis as the ratio of observed serve-rate vs committed rate over a monthly window, capped and normalized to tokens-per-minute. 3) Deferred burst policy: allow short-term bursts above committed rate up to a burst token budget (configurable per contract) that is amortized across a 24h sliding window; when burst budget exhausted, requests are prioritized by route tier and customer entitlement. 4) Crediting: proportional monetary credit tied to the percentage shortfall of the committed band, subject to a credit cap and minimum service thresholds. 5) Fleet controls: autoscaler interlock to avoid cascading throttles — signal priority to fleet controller and reserve a headroom pool for failed-AZ absorb. 6) Contract language appendix with example formulas and a short notice/escalation playbook.
acceptance_criteria: SLA definition doc published in Confluence with precise math for committed/ burst/elastic bands
Formal error budget calculation implemented in metrics pipeline and visible in Console dashboard (token-rate, 1h rolling quantiles)
Billing pipeline accepts credit events from measurement system and can issue proportional credits; two end-to-end test cases validated in staging
Autoscaler interlock implemented behind feature flag and validated under synthetic multi-AZ failover tests (load test report linked)
Legal sign-off on contract appendix language and sample customer amendment
Runbook created: detection, mitigation, customer notification templates, and post-incident credit computation steps
open_questions: Should the measurement window be 1h or 30m for tighter spike detection?
What is an acceptable credit cap as a percentage of monthly committed fees (10% vs 25%)?
How do we map route-level priorities to customer-visible route tiers without leaking internal cost signals?
If a customer requests a larger burst envelope, does price scale linearly or via a step function?
implementation_notes: Metric definition: committed_rate = contract_tokens_per_minute; observed_rate = median(tokens/minute) at 1h rolling quantile; shortfall = max(0, committed_rate - observed_rate); monthly_error_budget_percent = (sum(shortfall_minutes) / (committed_rate * minutes_in_month)) * 100
Burst budget: configurable burst_tokens_per_month; amortize as burst_tokens_per_24h = burst_tokens_per_month / 30; expiration = 24h sliding window
Crediting: credit_amount = min(billing_cap, contracted_monthly_fee * shortfall_percent * credit_multiplier); credit_multiplier defaults to 1.0 but can be escalated for repeated breaches
Autoscaler interlock: when observed AZ failure rate > threshold, reserve X% headroom from best-effort pool to preserve committed bands; expose telemetry for alerting and legal evidence
Test plan: multi-AZ teardown with synthetic traffic, validate console metrics and credit issuance in staging account ACCT-STG-DED-01
